title: Half of the government card does not say where the money went
intro: The Transparency Portal publishes every purchase made with the federal government's payment card: the agency, the date, the amount and the merchant. In 2025 there were 160,800 transactions and R$ 122.3 million. For almost half of the money, the merchant does not appear.
secretLabel: is marked "information protected by secrecy" — the amount shows, the destination does not
cashLabel: was withdrawn as cash from a government card, which by definition leaves no supplier trail
punch: The Ministry of Defence, which runs the armed forces, declared secrecy on 0.1% of what it spent on the card. The Presidency declared it on 98.3%.
honesty.title: Secrecy varies by agency
honesty.text: Two agencies that invoke security declared secrecy on 0.1% and on 98.3% of what they spent on the card. If secrecy followed from the activity, the two numbers would be close. R$ 50.6 million left your taxes without saying where it went. Which rule explains the difference?
question: If the Transparency Portal exists to show where the money went, what does it show when half the card comes marked as secret or leaves as cash?
source: Transparency Portal — Federal Government Payment Card, open files from January to December 2025
byOrg[0].org: Ministry of Justice and Public Security
byCash[1].org: Ministry of Justice and Public Security
byCash[2].org: Ministry of the Environment and Climate Change
mirror.text: You are required to declare where every real that entered your account came from, and omitting it carries a fine. The government marked 41% of what it spent on the card as secret — and the secrecy is not a failure: it is a category of the very system built to show the spending.
mirror.highlight: 41% of what it spent on the card as secret
mirror.source: Federal Revenue Service — the duty to declare, and the fine for omission on the income tax return
